 2                                 PERSONAL INFORMATION:

 3   Q. Please state your name and address.

 4   A. My name is Caroline R. Runge. My address is -3232 Runge Ranch Road, Fort

 5   McKavett, TX 76841


 6   Q. Have you filed a Motion to intervene in this proceeding?

 7   A. Yes.


 8   Q. What link and tracts are you testifying in representation of today?

 9   A. Links Rl and R2 in Schleicher County, Texas and link P3 in Menard County, Texas

10   Q. Are you testifying on behalf of anyone, or just yourself?

11   A.I am testifying on behalf of Runge Ranch Company, Richard S, Runge, Arthur S.

12   Runge, Edith May Kissko and myself.

13   Q. How is the property affected by the Bell County East to Big Hill 765kV

14   transmission line project proposed by Oncor and LCRA TSC?

15   A. Our ranch property in Schleicher County is crossed by both links Rl and R2. R2

16   crosses in the vicinity of the 100-year old house where our son lives, as well as the

17   barns, and working pens,and divides our ranch property through the middle of two

18   sections. Rl section of the ranch.

19   The Menard County ranch is crossed by link P3. across the northern two sections of the

20   ranch and passes close by the house where my husband and I live.
                                                              Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 4 of 14
  1   Q. What routes do you oppose?

 2   Links Rl and R2 in Schleicher County, and link P3 in Menard County.

 3   Q. What routes do you support?

 4   None, but would prefer Link Pl in Schleicher County and links P2 and P 42 in Menard

 5   County.

 6   Q. Have you ever testified at the Public Utility Commission of Texas before?

7    No.

 8   Q. Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision?

 g   yes.

10                                       EMINENT DOMAIN

11   Does the proposed LCRA-Oncor transmission line project meet the requirements

12   for Eminent Domain?


13   No. Texas Government Code Chapter 2206, Title 10, Subtitle E. Government property,

14   Subchapter A. on purpose and use of property acquired through Eminent Domain

15   Section 2206.001 Limitation on Eminent Domain for Private Parties or Economic

16   Development. Private property may not be taken by eminent domain "if the taking

17   confers a private benefit on a particular private party" or "is for a public use that is

18   merely a pretext to confer a private benefit on a particular private party." The publicized

19   large load requests are for data centers, crypto mining, battery storage and Permian

20   Basin oil extraction, all of which are privately owned and stand to make vast amounts of
                                                                Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                           Page 5 of 14
  1   money as a result of the enhanced supply of electricity at through the significant

 2   diminution of the value of private rural property along its route.

 3                            PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND HISTORY

 4   Q. Can you please describe the affected property, including the legal description

 5   from the County CAD?

 6   Schleicher County: 2240 acres of native pastureland, one residence, one barn, a few

 7   small outbuildings with agricultural use.

 6   Q. Can you please explain your history and familiarity with the affected property,

 7   including its current usage?

 8   A. The Schleicher County Ranch has been in our family for over 100 years, since 1923,

 9   and has been continuously used since then for raising livestock, primarily sheep, goats

10   and cattle. In the last forty years it has also been leased for seasonal game hunting,

11   including deer, turkeys and dove.

12   The oldest water well in the county was drilled on this property in 1882 by Christopher

13   Columbus Doty, often considered the first permanent resident of the county. The well is

14   still in use to water livestock. Near the well is a rock house, still standing, that was built

15   in the early 1890's (photo below).

16   The South Concho draw runs through the property and there are caves in the bluffs

17   above the draw where Native American arrowheads and other artifacts have been

18   found.

19   B. The Menard County Ranch has been in our family for 139 years, since 1887, and has

20   also been continuously used during that period for raising livestock, and for game

21   hunting during the last four decades. Richard S. Runge's grandfather, Robert Winslow,

22   was the original patentee of one of the sections and the ranch has been recognized as

23   a Texas Land Heritage ranch by the Texas Department of Agriculture.

 7                IMPACT ON LAND USE AND ECONOMICS (PURA 4 37.056)

 8   Q. How would the proposed transmission line interfere with your current land

 9   use?

10   A. We currently depend entirely on livestock ranching and leasing for deer hunting.

11   Proposed Line R2 crosses through the middle of our ranch in Schleicher County in the

12   vicinity of the house where our son lives and close to the historic water well. Line Rl

13   crosses through the northernmost section of the ranch.


                                                              Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 9 of 14
  1   Proposed line P3 crosses thorough our ranch in Menard County close to the house

 2   where my husband and I live.

 3   The sensory disturbance by the gigantic towers, the electromagnetic emissions, the UV

 4   corona visibility and the excessive noise from the lines will seriously affect both

 5   livestock and deer species as to reproduction and distribution, thus reducing

 6   productivjty.

 7   New medical evidence filed in 2026 by Dr. W. Ben Johnson (a retired Cardiac

 8   Electrophysiologist) shows that the 765 kV lines proposed for West Texas represent a

 9   5,011-fold increase in physical energy intensity compared to the natural background of

10   our ranchland.

11   "This isn't just "noise"-it is Mechanical Work being performed on every living cell within

12   a 1.5-mile radius of the line."

13   "The 120Hz tonal hum and crackle of these lines trigger a chronic elevation of stress

14   hormones which can result in decreased yields, impaired metabolic health, and

15   systemic oxidative stress in cattle."

16   Further, part of the attraction of the ranches to our deer hunters is the natural

17   environment devoid of industrial structures. Our hunters are allowed to come onto the

18   ranch all year long and many do, expressly to get away from the urban environments

19   where they live and work. It is likely that we will may those hunters, not only because of

20   the disturbance to the deer population but also because of the degradation of the

21   natural environment.. We would not be compensated for those very real damages to our

22   Iivelihood, either the livestock losses or deer hunting..

                                                                 Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                          Page 10 of 14
  1   Q. Are there any specific structures or features that would be within a half mile

 2   feet of any of the proposed routes?

 3   . It appears that the residences on both ranches are within a half mile of the proposed

4    routes, as are the historical well and rock house on the Schleicher County ranch.

 5   Q. In your opinion, how will this project affect the value of your land?

 6   Most of the sales of land in our counties now are for recreation, it no longer being

 7   economically feasible to buy land at current prices to raise livestock. Therefore a

 8   significant aspect of the value of our property to potential buyers is the peace and quiet

 9   and natural environment, all of which would be destroyed by the presence of the

10   structures, the noise they make and presence of people maintaining them. Further, the

11   likelihood of diminished deer hunting will also devalue the land.

12   WH[ landowners be adequately and fairly compensated for the taking of their

13   property?

14   Not even close. In 2012, when LCRA was installing a 345 kw CREZ line in Schleicher

15   and Menard counties, Florida Power and Light, a private company, was also building a

16   transmission line in Menard County. FP&L negotiated contracts with landowners for

17   acceptable payments, installed lines in locations that suited the landowners, and had

18   their line up and running two years before LCRA finally finished battling over payments

19   and locations. Even after protracted legal action, the LCRA didn't pay as much per

20   mile as FP&L paid in their arm-length transactions with landowners.



                                                              Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                             PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 11 of 14
  1   In addition, LCRA-Oncor will not pay compensation for the diminution of income

 2   resulting from disturbance to livestock and wildlife, nor for the stress and annoyance of

 3   having crews and equipment crossing our lands for construction and maintenance.

 4   It is unconscionable that the Iivelihoods and peaceful enjoyment of their property of

 5   rural Texas landowners are being sacrificed so that residents of more populated areas

 6   don't have these giant structures ruining their "viewshed" and that we receive

 7   inadequate one-time compensation when millions of dollars will be made for decades by

 8   private companies and individuals who are the benefactors of this enhanced electrical

 9   supply. At the very least the landowners who have to bear this burden involuntarily

10   should receive the equivalent of a royalty payment per kilowatt hour generated.

11   Will there be health hazards to landowners from the transmission line?

12   Utility structures of this size are new to the state - while it is already known that the

13   electromagnetic fields generated by the lines are damaging to humans, it is not known

14   to what extent. Further, the stress of seeing these structures on land that has been in

15   our family for 139 years on the Menard ranch and over 100 years on the Schleicher

16   ranch would be serious.

17   Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?

18   It is difficult to convey how very much the sight of these giant structures marching over

19   the terrain that we have loved, worked on to conserve and improve, and made our living

20   from for over a century, would be upsettjng on a dajly basjs, to say nothing of the

21   aggravation of crews and equipment coming on the property. Our family has been

                                                                Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 12 of 14
  1   through a lot of hard times to hang onto this land- the Depression, the drought of the

 2   Fifties, as well as the ongoing the struggles with drought, predators.etc. It would not be

 3   as bad with the Schleicher county ranch, as that is across Highway 277 from the Big

 4   Hill substation, and other transmission lines are visible, but it would be devastating on

 5   the Menard County ranch.

 6   Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use

 7   on your land?

 8   Definitely. We have done extensive estate planning to ensure that these ranches stay

 9   within the family and continue to be used for ranching for at least another two

10   generations. Some rural landowners may adjust or sell their land for less than they

11   would get otherwise and move on to other pursuits, but we have made Iongterm

12   arrangements for our children and grandchildren to carry on This transmission line

13   could truly wreck our family's future.

14              ENVIRONMENTAL AND AESTHETIC IMPACTS (16 TAC § 25.101)


15   Q. What are your concerns regarding the local environment and wildlife?

16   A.

17   Q. How will the line affect the "aesthetic values" (the look and feel) of your area?


18                         LOCAL NEED AND COST (PURA 4 37.056)

19   Q. Do you believe this project provides a direct benefit to your local electric

20   service?

                                                               Direct Testimony of {Caroline R. Runge
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                      SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 13 of 14
  1   No.

 2   Q. Do you believe this project will decrease your electric cost?

 3   No. On the contrary, I believe it will increase electric costs.

 4                          CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

 5   Q. What is your recommendation to the Commission?

 6   1.That the Commission deny the CCN for this LCRA-Oncor transmission line.

 7   2.Find that this line is not a legitimate public use, that it benefits private entities and is

 8   therefore not eligible to use of Eminent Domain.

 9   3. Require that large load enterprises like Permian basin extraction and data centers

10   develop local electric-generating sources which they fund themselves rather than

11   unduly burdening distant rural communities which receive no benefit from the

12   construction of the line..

13   4. Alternatively, that the routes Pl in Schleicher County and P2 and P42 in Menard

14   County be approved.

15   Q. Does this conclude your testimony?


16   A. Yes.
